Off track. Watch hours: 191 of 4,000, up 36 in 7 days (about 6 a day, down from 7.4). Reaching 4,000 by February needs about 37 a day, and the end-of-November target of 800 is out of reach.
Subscribers: 386, with +2 in 7 days and none since 11-13. The Shorts subscribe-line test (Exp F) failed, and the line comes out on 11-17.
Main reason: last week's long videos covered narrow topics (diarrhea, dehydration, pen, alcohol) and earned 137 minutes between them at days 3–6. Broad videos earn a median of 621 each. I chose those narrow topics. From now on, long videos answer broad, searched questions only.
Production: 5 of the last 12 long-video renders were held (3 for scenes out of sync with the voice), but backups covered all 7 days.
Shorts → long videos: still 0 views from Shorts or end screens on every long video.
For you, about 15 min in Studio: related-video links on 10 Shorts and end screens on EloraTZP, Side Effects and Stopping. Then the render sync fix, and swap the carousel days for a second long video.
bottleneck:
The bottleneck is getting new long videos discovered, and this week's topic choices made it worse.

**Narrow videos don't get shown.**
- The 4 new long videos that have data (Diarrhea 65 min, Dehydration 14, Pen 22, Alcohol 36) earned 137 minutes combined at days 3–6.
- Each had 193 impressions or fewer. Diarrhea got 0 views from suggested videos.
- They were narrow because last week's playbook queued single-symptom topics. The analyst's proven split (n=11) says the same: the 5 broad searched questions have a median of 621 minutes each, and the 6 narrow ones about 39.
- Ages differ, so the small numbers are partly age, but the impression ceiling is the real limit.

**Our watch time is almost all old videos.** About 6 hours a day come mostly from Side Effects (1,105 min), What to Eat (797), Stopping (350), How Long (264) and EloraTZP (about 44% of lifetime minutes). The new videos add almost nothing.

**Nothing moves viewers between our videos.**
- Views from Shorts and from end screens are 0 on every long video, and playlists have brought about 9 views in total.
- The related-video links on Shorts and the end screens are still not set. Exp G has been waiting 7 days.
- So our best videos send their viewers nowhere, and our winning Shorts (injection site 254 and 202, pen blood 111, hair-women 119) can't feed the matching long videos.

**Production losses.**
- 5 of the last 12 long-video renders were held or failed: 3 for scenes out of sync with the voice (11-09, 11-10, 11-14), 1 for audio (11-11) and 1 for a fact-check revision (11-14).
- On all 3 sync holds the plan had nearly every scene on time but the finished render had only 83–88%.
- Backups covered all 7 days, but held videos included a broad topic (Nausea Foods).
- The 13:00 ET Short was held 3 days out of 7 for audio, and that slot's news Shorts get about 25 views anyway.

**Subscribers.** +2 in 7 days, and the Shorts subscribe line added nothing. Long videos bring in subscribers about 10 times better per view than Shorts, so subscribers will follow long-video views, not Shorts wording.
playbook_markdown:
# InforMed growth playbook: week of 2026-11-17

**Status: off track.** 191 of 4,000 watch hours, at about 6 a day (February needs about 37). 386 subscribers, +2 in 7 days. New narrow long-forms earn almost nothing; the broad back catalogue earns. **This week: broad searched questions only, every day, and link everything.**

## Standing rules (owner, 2026-11-12; keep)
- Packaging keeps the gap. Titles and thumbnails never state the answer; state-change layouts are fine if the text keeps the question. The answer comes by 15 s (long) or 6 s (Shorts).
- Drug first. Shorts sentence 1 names tirzepatide (or the one drug the evidence is about) in ≤14 words, and scene 1's on-screen text matches it. Titles put the drug first.
- First frame is composed (character plus hook text at t=0). Shorts change shot at least every 2.5 s in the first 10 s. Never relax this.
- Long-form mix: Lane A is the base, plus 2–3 search-demand long videos a week: device how-to (Instructions for Use only, no amounts), what-to-expect timelines, label changes, approved-drug head-to-heads against tirzepatide. The "What is X?" ban covers unapproved pipeline drugs only.
- Shorts: at least 2 of 3 a day are a felt symptom or practical moment. A study supports a Short; it is never the topic.
- Shorts ending from 11-17: one short safety line, then a line that loops into the first. Never "link in the description" in a Short.

## Long-form (14:00 ET, 9–11 min)
- **Broad only.** Title it "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) …" plus a broad searched question, ≤55 characters. No new single-symptom or single-interaction long-forms; those go into Shorts or chapters.
- Order, one a day. If a video is held, ship the next ready one; never leave the day empty.
  1. Nausea: Foods That May Help. Re-render the verified 11-14 script from the final word timestamps; no script change.
  2. Mounjaro vs Zepbound: What's Different? (search-demand; US labels only)
  3. Weight Loss: How Much in the Trials? (both arms, full trial population, no dose advice)
  4. Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill: What to Expect. Regenerate the broken audio scene from the 11-11 script (search-demand, label only).
  5. Months 2–6: What to Expect (sequel to First Month; label plus trial averages)
  6. Serious Risks: How Rare? Apply the 11-14 fact-check REVISE fixes and resubmit.
  7. Zepbound Vial vs Pen (search-demand; Instructions for Use only, no amounts), and only if the real IFU URL loads.
- Backups (re-render; ship only on a held day): Injection Site Reactions (11-09), Burping and Heartburn (11-10).
- Ship-blockers, unchanged:
  - every cut within 0.5 s of its beat, measured on the render
  - masking 0.02 or lower, measured on the final file
  - transcript matches the script word for word
  - the description ends "…whether it's right for you."
  - The fact-checker and the Editor-in-Chief always win.

## Script structure (long-form; Exp H)
- Sentence 1: the drug plus the title's question. Short answer by 15 s, then a "you" scenario.
- **Second concrete payoff at 15–30 s** (a number or the first step). Keep the open loop to one sentence.
- Land a payoff before about 70 s; chapter 2 opens with a question. Re-hook every 45–75 s.
- Land the last payoff before the recap. One subscribe ask, after the payoff. End with "There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description." Never say "on screen".

## Linking (copywriter and publisher)
- The copywriter leaves line 1 empty. The publisher fills it with a verified ▶ Watch next link.
- Targets:
  - each new broad video → Side Effects
  - Side Effects → Stopping
  - Stopping → Keeping Results
  - Keeping Results → Stopping
  - First Month → Months 2–6 once it's live (How Long until then)
  - Pen → Side Effects
  - Mounjaro vs Zepbound and Foundayo → How It Works
  - EloraTZP → Side Effects
- Add the line-1 link to the existing EloraTZP, Side Effects, Stopping, How Long and First Month descriptions. **Don't touch Strength or What to Eat until 11-24 (Exp E).**
- Playlists: every Lane A video goes in "Life on Tirzepatide". Also make a series playlist "Your First Months on Tirzepatide" with First Month, Months 2–6 and How Long.
- Retitle the Hair Loss long video (0.93% CTR): "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Hair Loss: Why More in Women?"
- Fix the 11-15 L1 pinned comment so it gives SURMOUNT-4's full trial population, not "adults".

## Shorts (08:00 / 13:00 / 20:00 ET)
- Length and hook style: follow the task's `short-length` arm and `hook-archetype`; never override them. Never more than 160 spoken words.
- **08:00:** a visible body or pen moment, "Is this normal?". Current winners: injection site 254 and 202, pen blood 111, hair in women 119.
- **13:00:** also a practical moment. News Shorts in this slot sit at about 25 views. Only exception: a fresh randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide in an obesity population.
- **20:00, 11-18 to 11-27:** the holiday table: full fast, heartburn, drinks at a party, leftovers, travelling with the pen (storage per the label). Target: the Thanksgiving or What to Eat long video.
- Every Short logs one target long video in its post notes for the owner's related-video link (Exp G):
  - pen or injection → Pen how-to
  - hair → Hair Loss
  - stomach → Side Effects
  - food or holiday → Thanksgiving
- **Exp F has ended:** from 11-17, drop the subscribe line and "Full breakdown… link in the description".
- Banned:
  - "3 Ways" lists and approval-status titles
  - cost, Medicare and pharmacy topics; surgery; grocery
  - observational or survey studies as the topic
  - brand-first titles, and semaglutide-only titles unless the evidence is semaglutide-only

## Carousels
- Make one only if the scheduler asks, and reuse verified Short text only.

## Analyst
- Exp H: 30-second hold and midpoint retention at day 7 for every long-form from 11-11 on.
- Search-demand vs Lane A at day 14: Pen on 11-25, First Month on 11-27.
- Exp E on 11-24, short-length on 11-26, and hook-archetype once each style has n≥8.
- Confirm the 11-14 "How It Works" long video is live; it's missing from the snapshot.
- Log views from Shorts on each target long video from the day its related-video link is set.

experiments.name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail (What to Eat, plus Strength as a second test)
experiments.hypothesis: Our two most-shown practical videos have a packaging problem, not a discovery problem. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer that keeps the question lifts CTR toward 3.8–4.7%.
experiments.change: Only the thumbnail changes, with no body imagery. What to Eat was swapped around 11-04 and Strength on 11-10. No other edits to either video until 11-24, including description links and end screens.
experiments.metric: CTR on impressions after the swap vs CTR just before it (What to Eat about 1.9%, Strength about 0.6%), with views per day not falling. Success: 3.0%+ on both.
experiments.min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days per video, whichever comes later (read on 11-24)
experiments.result: Not readable yet. What to Eat moved only from about 790 to 797 lifetime minutes this week. Strength is still earning a little. Read on 11-24 against the before-swap rate, not the overall average.

experiments.name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double how often Shorts viewers subscribe.
experiments.change: The 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts ended with 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' The 20:00 Shorts were the control.
experiments.metric: Subscribers per 1,000 views at day 7, line vs control, and channel subscribers per day vs the 1.3-a-day baseline. Success: 2× the control and 2.5+ a day.
experiments.result: Lost. Channel subscribers went from 382 (11-03) to 386 (11-16): about 0.3 a day, against a 1.3 baseline and a 2.5 target. Every Short with per-Short data shows 0 subscribers, with or without the line. The last day can't change the result. This is confounded by Shorts views falling to about half the baseline, but nothing points to a lift. The line comes out from 11-17, when the owner's new Shorts ending takes over.

experiments.name: Exp G: Studio related-video link on top Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: The related-video link is the only clickable path from a Short. Setting it on our best body and pen Shorts, aimed at the long video on the same topic, will create Shorts traffic to long videos that converts to subscribers.
experiments.change:
The owner sets one related-video link per Short, with targets matched by topic:
- hair grow-back (1,025) and hair in women (119) → Hair Loss
- injection site (254), injection sites (202), pen blood (111) and pen out of the fridge (11-15) → Pen how-to
- nausea (190) → Side Effects
- bones (249) → Bones & Muscle
- breakfast (134) → What to Eat
- Thanksgiving (11-06) → Thanksgiving
No other change to these Shorts.
experiments.metric: Views and minutes from Shorts on each target long video in the 7 days after the link is set, vs 0 before. Success: at least 1 long-video view per 100 new Short views across the set, plus a visible rise in channel subscribers.
experiments.min_sample: 8 linked Shorts, 7 days after the links are set
experiments.result: Not started. The links still aren't set after 7 days, and views from Shorts are still 0 on every long video. The targets were updated now that the Hair Loss and Pen long videos are live; the test starts the day the owner sets the links.

experiments.name: Exp H: Second payoff at 15–30 s in long-form scripts
experiments.hypothesis: The biggest drop comes at 12–35 s (14 of 19 curves), right after the first answer. A second concrete payoff (a number or the first step) at 15–30 s, with an open loop of one sentence at most, lifts the 30-second hold and the midpoint hold.
experiments.change: Every long video from the 11-11 Pen video onward uses this structure. Nothing else in the script template changes.
experiments.metric: Day-7 median hold at 30 s and median relative hold at the midpoint, vs the n=19 baseline (30-second hold about 77%, midpoint 43.6). Success: 30-second hold of 82%+ and midpoint of 48+.
experiments.min_sample: 6 long videos built this way, at day 7
experiments.result: Started on 11-11. Pen is read on 11-18 and Alcohol on 11-19. Early anecdote: average view percentage of 63% for Pen and 67% for Alcohol at days 3–4, against a long-form norm of about 45%. Too few and too early to judge.

experiments.name: short-length (owner): tight vs standard Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: Tighter Shorts (90–120 words, 40–55 s) earn more views and a higher average view percentage than standard ones (135–160 words, 65–80 s).
experiments.change: Each Short's task sets `tight` or `standard`, alternating by slot and day, from 11-12 to 11-26.
experiments.metric: Median views and average view percentage per arm at day 7.
experiments.min_sample: All Shorts from 11-12 to 11-26 (about 20 per arm), each at day 7
experiments.result: No read until 11-26. Record the winner in the playbook then.

experiments.name: hook-archetype (owner): opening style for Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: Some of the 5 opening styles (result-first, negation, number-first, myth-flip, recognition-question) beat the others on views and average view percentage.
experiments.metric: Median views and average view percentage per style at day 7.
experiments.result: No style has n≥8 yet. Don't read it.

experiments.name: Search-demand long videos vs Lane A (owner)
experiments.hypothesis: Device how-to, what-to-expect, label-change and approved-drug head-to-head long videos bring more search views and minutes than Lane A videos of the same age.
experiments.change: 2–3 of the week's long videos are search-demand videos, starting with Pen (11-11) and First Month (11-13). This week: Mounjaro vs Zepbound, Foundayo What to Expect, Zepbound Vial vs Pen.
experiments.metric: Minutes and search views at day 14, matched by age.
experiments.result: Too early. Anecdote: Pen had 22 min on 17 views at day 4, and 8 of its 12 non-subscriber views came from search. Search pulls in viewers, but the volume is small so far. First readouts: Pen on 11-25, First Month on 11-27.

owner_decisions:
**Set the related-video links on 10 Shorts in YouTube Studio (Exp G; about 10 minutes, needs advanced features turned on).**
- Hair grow-back (1,025 views) and hair in women (119) → Hair Loss long.
- Injection site (254), injection sites (202), pen blood (111) and pen out of the fridge (11-15) → Pen how-to long.
- Nausea (190) → Side Effects. Bones (249) → Bones & Muscle. Breakfast (134) → What to Eat. Thanksgiving Short (11-06) → Thanksgiving long.

Why: views from Shorts are 0 on all 30 long videos, and this link is the only clickable path out of a Short. Our Shorts have 14,154 views in 90 days and send none of them to a long video.

Expected effect: modest. At the 1-per-100 success bar it's a few long views a day at first. But long videos bring in subscribers about 10 times better per view than Shorts, and the link keeps working with no further effort.

**Add end screens in YouTube Studio:**
- EloraTZP → Side Effects and Stopping
- Side Effects → Stopping and Bones & Muscle
- Stopping → Keeping Results
- First Month → How Long
Leave Strength and What to Eat alone until 11-24 (Exp E).

Why: EloraTZP has about 44% of our lifetime long-video minutes and an 8.12% CTR on 7,809 impressions, and Side Effects is our biggest practical earner (1,105 min). Today both send viewers nowhere. End-screen traffic is 0 on every long video.

Expected effect: end-screen clicks are usually low single-digit percentages of viewers. But this is the only lever on our biggest-earning videos and it lasts. Each viewer it moves watches about 5–7 minutes of a Lane A video.

**Fix render-time beat sync in the pipeline (engineering).** Time every cut from the final word timestamps after the last audio is regenerated, and measure each beat's offset in the finished file.

Why: 3 long videos were dropped this cycle for scenes out of sync with the voice (11-09, 11-10, 11-14). Their plans had 96–100% of beats on time, but the renders had only 83–88%. One of them was a broad topic (Nausea Foods).

Also tighten the masking gate so it measures the final file: 0.022 shipped on 11-15 against a 0.02 limit.

Expected effect: about 3 more finished long videos a week. A broad Lane A video is worth roughly 4–18 watch hours in its first month.

**Remove the 17:30 carousel slot (carouselDays Tue/Fri in config/channel.json) and use that production run for a second long video on Tue and Fri at 22:00 ET.** 22:00 keeps the 8-hour spacing rule from the 14:00 slot. Publish the second video only when both pass QA, and each one must be a distinct broad topic.

Why: about 60 carousels have reached 0–4 people each (11-10 and 11-13 reached 0–1). Meanwhile watch hours depend on how many broad long videos we have live, and they are growing at only about 6 hours a day.

Expected effect: +2 broad long videos a week, roughly +8 to +36 watch hours a month per video pair, at no extra cost.
